Interpreted through the macro-finance literature, this FOMC statement conveys a credibility-preserving but cautious stance. Holding the federal funds rate at 5.25–5.50% and continuing QT is consistent with modern interest-rate implementation (Goodfriend; Woodford’s interest-rate policy view) and the Taylor principle, given inflation remains above target. The emphasis on “greater confidence” before easing addresses time-inconsistency and inflation-bias concerns (Barro–Gordon; Rogoff’s conservative central banker), supporting well-anchored expectations in the spirit of inflation forecast targeting (Svensson; Svensson–Woodford). With real economic activity expanding and unemployment low—implying a possible positive output gap—the New Keynesian Phillips curve/Calvo framework cautions against premature loosening, even as inflation has eased. Net tone: slightly positive on disinflation progress and improving risk balance, but still hawkish overall due to elevated inflation and commitment to the 2% objective and balance-sheet runoff.
